Marathon Petroleum stock rose 0.31% today to close at $388.90, extending a strong two-week run of nearly 8%. The gains reflect a tightening refining environment: refineries are running at 98% capacity, diesel inventories are at historically low levels, and diesel prices have hit record highs as conflicts in Ukraine and Iran have knocked Russian refineries offline. For a U.S. refiner, constrained global supply and high product prices mean stronger margins on fuel they produce and sell.

The broader backdrop amplifies this. Geopolitical escalation — Iran sanctions intensifying, the war in Ukraine worsening, and moves to control the Strait of Hormuz — is crimping global oil refining capacity precisely when U.S. refiners have the room to run hard. With oil at $91–96 a barrel and storage levels relatively balanced, the refining sector is positioned to benefit from the supply-demand mismatch in refined products.
